description: Placement-focused MCQs for Software Developer / Software Engineer preparation.

questions.question: Which OOP concept lets a class reuse behavior defined by another class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance lets a subclass reuse or extend members of a superclass.

questions.question: Which concept bundles data and related methods and controls access to internal state?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation groups state and behavior and controls access to internal details.

questions.question: What is an object in object-oriented programming?
questions.explanation: An object is an instance of a class with state and behavior.

questions.question: What is a class?
questions.explanation: A class defines the structure and behavior of its instances.

questions.question: Which concept exposes essential behavior while hiding implementation details?
questions.explanation: Abstraction presents a simplified interface while hiding implementation details.

questions.question: What is method overriding?

options.A: Using the same name for unrelated variables
options.B: Providing a subclass implementation of an inherited method
options.C: Deleting a method at compile time

questions.explanation: Overriding lets a subtype customize inherited behavior, subject to language rules.

questions.question: In Java, which feature is commonly used to achieve compile-time polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Overloaded methods are selected using their parameter signatures at compile time.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a constructor?
questions.explanation: A constructor initializes an object's state when it is created.

questions.question: Which SOLID principle says a class should have one reason to change?
questions.explanation: SRP recommends that a module have one primary responsibility or reason to change.

questions.question: Which principle recommends depending on abstractions rather than concrete implementations?
questions.explanation: DIP reduces coupling by making high-level and low-level modules depend on abstractions.

questions.question: What does the Liskov Substitution Principle require?

options.A: Subtypes should preserve the behavioral expectations of their base types
options.B: Every class must have two constructors

questions.explanation: Subtypes should remain usable wherever their base types are expected without breaking correctness.

questions.question: What is an interface primarily used for?

options.A: Defining a contract implementations can provide

questions.explanation: An interface specifies operations that implementing types agree to provide.

questions.question: What is the difference between an instance method and a static method in many OOP languages?

options.A: An instance method is associated with an object; a static method belongs to the type
options.B: Static methods always use more memory

questions.explanation: Instance methods usually operate on an instance, while static methods are associated with the class or type.

questions.question: Which data structure follows Last In, First Out (LIFO)?
questions.explanation: A stack removes the most recently added element first.

questions.question: Which data structure normally follows First In, First Out (FIFO)?
questions.explanation: A standard queue removes elements in the order they were inserted.

questions.question: Which structure typically supports direct indexed access to elements?
questions.explanation: Arrays typically support constant-time indexed access.

questions.question: What is the average lookup complexity of a well-distributed hash table?
questions.explanation: Hash-table lookup is expected O(1) on average, although worst cases can be slower.

questions.question: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits keys in sorted order when the BST property holds?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal visits the left subtree, node, then right subtree.

questions.question: Which data structure is commonly used to implement breadth-first search?
questions.explanation: BFS processes discovered vertices in first-in-first-out order.

questions.question: Which data structure is commonly used by iterative depth-first search?
questions.explanation: An explicit stack supports DFS; recursive DFS uses the call stack.

questions.question: What is a common advantage of a linked list over an array?

options.B: Insertion or deletion can be O(1) when the node position is already known

questions.explanation: Once the position is known, relinking can insert or remove a node in O(1) time.

questions.question: What is the worst-case search complexity in an unbalanced binary search tree with n nodes?
questions.explanation: An unbalanced tree can degrade into a chain, requiring linear search time.

questions.question: What is the defining property of a max-heap?

options.A: Every node is smaller than its children
options.B: Each parent is greater than or equal to its children
options.D: It is always a binary search tree

questions.explanation: A max-heap maintains each parent greater than or equal to its children.

questions.question: Which data structure is useful for efficiently retrieving the highest-priority item?
questions.explanation: A priority queue returns items according to priority, often using a heap.

questions.question: Which algorithm searches a sorted array in O(log n) time?
questions.explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves the remaining sorted search interval.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search through n elements?
questions.explanation: The target may be absent or last, requiring inspection of every element.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort has logarithmic levels and linear merging work per level.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of bubble sort?
questions.explanation: Standard bubble sort uses quadratic comparisons in the worst case.

questions.question: Which strategy splits a problem into smaller subproblems and combines their solutions?
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer divides a problem, solves subproblems, and combines results.

questions.question: Which technique stores solutions to overlapping subproblems to avoid recomputation?
questions.explanation: Dynamic programming reuses stored subproblem results.

questions.question: Which approach makes a locally optimal choice at each step?
questions.explanation: Greedy algorithms choose locally optimal steps; correctness depends on the problem.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of quicksort with consistently poor pivots?
questions.explanation: Highly unbalanced partitions can produce quadratic work.

questions.question: Which graph algorithm finds shortest paths from one source when edge weights are nonnegative?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm computes single-source shortest paths for nonnegative edge weights.

questions.question: Which algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by adding low-weight edges that do not create cycles?
questions.explanation: Kruskal sorts edges and adds those that do not create cycles.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a compiler?

options.A: Translate source code into a target representation

questions.explanation: A compiler translates source code into machine code or an intermediate representation.

questions.question: Which construct is primarily used to branch based on a condition?
questions.explanation: An if statement executes a branch depending on whether its condition is true.

questions.question: What is recursion?

options.A: A function calling itself directly or indirectly

questions.explanation: Recursive code calls itself and needs a termination condition.

questions.question: What is a common purpose of exception handling?

options.A: Handle exceptional runtime conditions in a controlled way

questions.explanation: Exception handling allows software to respond to errors or exceptional conditions.

questions.question: What is a variable?

options.A: A named storage location or binding for a value

questions.explanation: Variables provide names for values or storage according to language semantics.

questions.question: What is the difference between syntax and semantics?

options.A: Syntax concerns grammatical form; semantics concerns meaning or behavior
options.B: Syntax means speed; semantics means memory

questions.explanation: Syntax defines valid structure, while semantics defines what the structure means.

questions.question: What does Big O notation commonly express in algorithm analysis?

options.A: An asymptotic upper bound on growth
options.B: Exact runtime in seconds on all machines

questions.explanation: Big O describes an asymptotic upper bound on a function's growth.

questions.question: What is the typical time complexity of indexed access in an array?
questions.explanation: An array index can usually be converted directly into an element address.

questions.question: If an algorithm scans every element of an n-element array once, what is its time complexity?
questions.explanation: A single pass performs work proportional to n.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of unit testing?

options.A: Test small units of code independently where practical

questions.explanation: Unit tests check individual units and help detect defects early.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of version control?

options.A: Track changes and coordinate work on files over time
options.B: Run source code in every language

questions.explanation: Version control records changes, supports collaboration, and helps recover prior versions.

questions.question: What does continuous integration typically involve?

options.A: Frequently integrating changes with automated builds and tests

questions.explanation: CI frequently builds and tests integrated changes to detect problems early.

questions.question: What is a good first step when investigating a reproducible defect?

options.A: Reproduce the issue and isolate the cause

questions.explanation: Reproducing and isolating the issue makes debugging systematic.

questions.question: What is a process?

options.A: A program in execution with its execution context and resources

questions.explanation: A process is a running instance of a program managed by the operating system.

questions.question: What is a thread?

options.A: A unit of execution within a process

questions.explanation: Threads are execution units within a process and may share process resources.

questions.question: What does HTTP primarily define?

options.A: A protocol for transferring web resources

questions.explanation: HTTP is an application-layer protocol used for web communication.

questions.question: What does SQL stand for?
questions.explanation: SQL is used to define, query, and manipulate relational data.

questions.question: Why should passwords be stored using a password-hashing algorithm with a unique salt?

options.A: To make recovering original passwords from a database leak harder
options.B: To make passwords visible to administrators
options.D: To store passwords in plain text

questions.explanation: A unique salt and password-specific hashing make offline password cracking more difficult.

questions.question: Which principle recommends that software entities be open for extension but closed for modification?
questions.explanation: The Open/Closed Principle encourages extending behavior without repeatedly modifying stable existing code.

questions.question: A subtype cannot honor the behavioral expectations of its parent type. Which principle is at risk?
questions.explanation: LSP requires subtypes to remain usable where the base type is expected.

questions.question: What does dependency injection primarily do?

options.A: Supplies dependencies from outside a component
options.B: Hard-codes every dependency inside a class

questions.explanation: Dependency injection separates dependency construction from dependency use.

questions.question: What is an immutable object?

options.A: An object whose observable state cannot change after construction
options.C: An object stored only on disk
options.D: An object that must be global

questions.explanation: Immutability prevents state changes after an object is created.

questions.question: Which pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface?
questions.explanation: The Strategy pattern makes algorithms interchangeable through a shared contract.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a disjoint-set union structure?

options.A: Track connected components under union operations

questions.explanation: Union-find tracks partitions and merges sets efficiently.

questions.question: Which structure is well suited to prefix lookup over many strings?
questions.explanation: A trie organizes keys by shared prefixes.

questions.question: What is a circular queue designed to do?

options.A: Reuse positions by wrapping around a buffer

questions.explanation: A circular queue reuses buffer positions after elements are removed.

questions.question: Which representation can be space-efficient for a sparse graph?

options.B: Full adjacency matrix in every case

questions.explanation: Adjacency lists use space proportional to vertices plus edges.

questions.question: What is a common advantage of a balanced search tree?
questions.explanation: Self-balancing rules keep tree height logarithmic.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time and can be stable?
questions.explanation: Merge sort has O(n log n) worst-case time and can preserve the order of equal keys.

questions.question: Which technique explores candidate choices and abandons a path when constraints are violated?
questions.explanation: Backtracking explores choices and prunes invalid partial solutions.

questions.question: Which algorithm is commonly used to find strongly connected components in a directed graph?
questions.explanation: Kosaraju's algorithm uses graph traversals to find strongly connected components.

questions.question: Which string-matching algorithm uses prefix information to avoid rechecking characters?
questions.explanation: KMP uses a prefix table to skip redundant comparisons.

questions.question: What does topological sorting produce for a directed acyclic graph?

options.A: A linear order respecting every directed edge
options.C: A sorted list of edge weights only
options.D: A shortest path for every weighted graph

questions.explanation: In a topological order, each directed edge goes from an earlier vertex to a later vertex.

questions.question: What is a pure function in the usual functional-programming sense?

options.A: A function whose result depends on its inputs and has no observable side effects
options.B: A function that changes global state every call
options.C: A function that must access the network
options.D: A function with no return value by definition

questions.explanation: A pure function is deterministic for the same inputs and has no observable side effects.

questions.question: Why should a function validate external input?

options.A: To reject or handle invalid data before it causes incorrect behavior
options.B: To make invalid data correct automatically
options.D: To ensure every input is numeric

questions.explanation: Validation establishes assumptions before data is used.

questions.question: What is a common benefit of meaningful variable names?

options.C: Automatic memory safety in every language

questions.explanation: Descriptive names help readers understand intent.

questions.question: What is an off-by-one error?

options.A: A boundary mistake that uses an index or count one too high or low

questions.explanation: Off-by-one errors commonly arise from incorrect loop bounds or index calculations.

questions.question: Why should a program avoid swallowing exceptions silently?

options.A: It can hide failures and make diagnosis difficult

questions.explanation: Silent exception suppression can conceal failures and leave a system in an unexpected state.

questions.question: What is the complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search interval at each step.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into a dynamic array when resizing requires copying elements?
questions.explanation: A resize may require copying all existing elements, making that insertion O(n).

questions.question: What does amortized analysis describe?

options.A: Average cost per operation over a sequence under a defined model
options.B: Exact cost of every operation on every machine

questions.explanation: Amortized analysis bounds the average cost over a sequence of operations.

questions.question: An algorithm stores one table entry per input item. What is the table's space complexity?
questions.explanation: One entry for each of n inputs uses linear space.

questions.question: What is the typical complexity of comparing every pair of n items?
questions.explanation: The number of pairs grows proportionally to n squared.

questions.question: What does refactoring aim to do?

options.A: Improve internal structure without intentionally changing external behavior
options.B: Add features by changing every interface

questions.explanation: Refactoring improves code structure while preserving externally observable behavior.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a pull request?

options.A: Propose changes for review before integrating them
options.D: Guarantee code is correct without review

questions.explanation: Pull requests provide a workflow for reviewing and discussing changes before merging.

questions.question: Why is separation of concerns useful?

options.A: It keeps distinct responsibilities from becoming unnecessarily entangled
options.B: It requires all code in one file

questions.explanation: Separating concerns makes components easier to understand, test, and change.

questions.question: What does semantic versioning commonly communicate?

options.A: Compatibility expectations through major, minor, and patch version numbers

questions.explanation: Semantic versioning communicates the nature of changes through version components.

questions.question: What is a technical debt trade-off?

options.A: A shortcut can speed delivery now but increase future maintenance cost
options.C: It refers only to unpaid invoices
options.D: It means testing is never needed

questions.explanation: Technical debt describes future costs introduced by expedient design or implementation choices.

questions.question: What is a mutex used for?

options.A: Mutual exclusion when accessing a protected resource

questions.explanation: A mutex helps ensure only one thread at a time enters a protected critical section.

questions.question: What is a semaphore commonly used to coordinate?

options.A: Access to resources or signaling between tasks

questions.explanation: Semaphores use a counter for coordination or resource permits.

questions.question: What is a page fault?

options.A: An event raised when a memory access requires page handling by the OS

questions.explanation: A page fault occurs when the requested virtual-memory page needs OS handling.

questions.question: What is a system call?

options.A: A controlled request for an operating-system service
options.B: A call to a method in every case

questions.explanation: System calls provide a boundary for requesting OS-managed operations.

questions.question: What is starvation in scheduling?

options.A: A task waits excessively because it is repeatedly denied needed resources or CPU time
options.C: A disk becomes full by definition

questions.explanation: Starvation occurs when a task is continually prevented from making progress.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of DHCP in typical IP networks?

options.A: Automatically provide network configuration such as IP addresses

questions.explanation: DHCP leases network configuration to clients.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used to send email between mail servers?
questions.explanation: SMTP is commonly used to relay email between mail servers.

questions.question: What is a subnet mask used for in IPv4 networking?

options.A: Distinguish network and host portions of an address

questions.explanation: A subnet mask indicates which address bits identify the network prefix.

questions.question: What does a load balancer commonly do?

options.A: Distributes requests across multiple backend instances

questions.explanation: Load balancers distribute traffic to improve capacity and availability.

questions.question: What does a firewall primarily enforce?

options.A: Network traffic rules based on configured policies

questions.explanation: Firewalls allow or block traffic according to security policy.

questions.question: What is normalization intended to reduce in relational database design?
questions.explanation: Normalization organizes relations to reduce redundant data and anomalies.

questions.question: What is a foreign key used for?

options.A: Enforce or represent a relationship to referenced key values

questions.explanation: Foreign keys help preserve referential integrity.

questions.question: What is a database transaction?

options.A: A logical unit of work that is committed or rolled back

questions.explanation: Transactions group database operations into a unit governed by transaction semantics.

questions.question: Why can an index slow down writes?

options.A: The index must also be maintained when indexed data changes
options.D: Indexes always require a full table scan

questions.explanation: Inserts, updates, and deletes may require index updates in addition to table changes.

questions.question: What is a database deadlock?

options.A: Transactions wait on resources held by one another in a cycle
options.C: A table has a primary key

questions.explanation: Deadlocks occur when transactions form a cycle of resource waits.

questions.question: What does multi-factor authentication require?

options.A: Two or more different factor categories
options.B: Two passwords from the same category only

questions.explanation: MFA combines distinct factor categories such as knowledge, possession, and inherence.

questions.question: What is phishing?

options.A: A deceptive attempt to trick people into revealing information or taking unsafe actions

questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages or sites to steal information or prompt unsafe actions.

questions.question: Why should software dependencies be updated and monitored?

options.A: To address known vulnerabilities and compatibility issues
options.C: To remove the need for backups

questions.explanation: Maintaining dependencies helps remediate known security issues and bugs.

questions.question: What is a secure default configuration?

options.A: A configuration that starts with restrictive, safer settings unless access is deliberately enabled
options.B: A configuration with all ports open
options.C: A password saved in source code

questions.explanation: Secure defaults reduce unnecessary exposure when systems are first deployed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of server-side input validation?

options.A: Check incoming data against expected types, formats, and constraints
options.D: Guarantee that a user is honest

questions.explanation: Server-side validation enforces application rules regardless of client-side checks.

questions.question: A test checks a function's behavior for one small, isolated unit. What kind of test is it?
questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on small units such as functions or classes.

questions.question: A test verifies that two services communicate correctly. What type of testing is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Integration testing checks interactions between components or services.

questions.question: A system is tested under many concurrent users. What is being evaluated?
questions.explanation: Load testing evaluates system behavior under expected or high workloads.

questions.question: A test succeeds locally but fails in CI because of hidden environment assumptions. What improvement is useful?

options.A: Make dependencies and test setup reproducible

questions.explanation: Reproducible environments reduce differences between local and CI execution.

questions.question: What is a mock commonly used for in unit testing?

options.A: Replace a dependency with a controlled test double

questions.explanation: Mocks simulate dependency behavior and help isolate the unit under test.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a payment service supports card and wallet implementations through the same operation. Which concept enables this?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism lets different implementations be used through a common contract.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a service must remove the earliest submitted request first. Which structure fits?
questions.explanation: A queue uses FIFO order.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, an array is sorted and a fast search is needed. Which algorithm should be used?
questions.explanation: Binary search runs in O(log n) time on sorted random-access data.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of a problem. What is this technique?
questions.explanation: Recursion solves a problem through calls to the same function.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a loop visits n elements once. What is its time complexity if each iteration is constant time?
questions.explanation: One constant-time operation per element yields linear time.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the main goal of refactoring?

options.A: Improve internal design without intentionally changing observable behavior

questions.explanation: Refactoring improves structure while preserving behavior.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a process?

options.A: A running program with its execution context and resources

questions.explanation: A process is an executing program managed by the operating system.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which service resolves domain names to IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS resolves domain names into resource records including IP addresses.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which SQL clause filters individual rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what helps prevent SQL injection in application queries?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries keep data separate from SQL syntax.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what does a unit test focus on?

options.A: A small software unit in isolation where practical

questions.explanation: Unit tests target small components such as functions or classes.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a class exposes private state through validated methods. Which concept is being applied?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation controls access to state through a defined interface.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a parser needs to match nested parentheses. Which structure is useful?
questions.explanation: A stack tracks the most recently opened delimiter.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a graph has unweighted edges and shortest paths by number of edges are needed. Which algorithm fits?
questions.explanation: BFS explores an unweighted graph in distance layers.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a common purpose of a return statement?

options.A: Send control and optionally a value back to the caller
options.D: Start a new process in every language

questions.explanation: Return ends a function call and may provide a result.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a loop halves its remaining input each iteration. What is its typical complexity?
questions.explanation: The number of halvings required is logarithmic.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, why use version control?

options.A: Track history and collaborate safely on changes
options.D: Eliminate the need for code review

questions.explanation: Version control records changes and supports collaboration and rollback.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a thread?

options.A: An execution unit within a process

questions.explanation: Threads execute within a process and typically share its address space.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which transport protocol provides a reliable ordered byte stream?
questions.explanation: TCP provides reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which SQL clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.explanation: HAVING applies conditions to groups created by GROUP BY.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what helps prevent cross-site scripting when rendering untrusted text?
questions.explanation: Output encoding prevents untrusted text from being interpreted as executable markup.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which testing checks communication between components?
questions.explanation: Integration tests verify interactions among components.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a subclass provides its own implementation of an inherited method. What is this?
questions.explanation: Overriding customizes inherited behavior in a subtype.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a dictionary needs expected constant-time lookup by key. Which structure is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Hash tables offer expected O(1) lookup under suitable assumptions.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a problem contains overlapping subproblems. Which technique can reuse their answers?
questions.explanation: Dynamic programming stores results of overlapping subproblems.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a loop should process items until none remain. Which approach is appropriate?

options.A: Loop with a clear termination condition
options.D: Use a class name as a condition

questions.explanation: A clear termination condition prevents unintended infinite loops.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, two nested loops each iterate n times. What is the overall complexity for constant-time work inside?
questions.explanation: The inner body executes approximately n squared times.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a pull request commonly used for?

options.D: Prove the code has no bugs

questions.explanation: Pull requests enable discussion and review before changes are integrated.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what can cause a race condition?

options.A: Unsynchronized concurrent access to shared mutable state

questions.explanation: Concurrent operations without proper coordination can produce timing-dependent results.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the common meaning of HTTP status 404?
questions.explanation: 404 indicates the requested resource was not found.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the purpose of a primary key?

options.B: Allow duplicate values in every row

questions.explanation: A primary key enforces unique identity for each row.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the principle of least privilege?

options.A: Grant only permissions needed for a task

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits potential damage from errors or compromised accounts.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is boundary-value analysis?

options.A: Testing values at and near limits

questions.explanation: Boundary values are common locations for defects.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a component should accept any implementation satisfying a contract. What should it use?
questions.explanation: An interface lets callers work with multiple compatible implementations.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a system repeatedly needs the smallest element. Which structure can efficiently provide it?

options.D: Unordered linked list without a maintained order

questions.explanation: A min-heap exposes the minimum at its root.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a minimum spanning tree is required for a connected weighted undirected graph. Which is appropriate?

options.D: Dijkstra for a single-source shortest path

questions.explanation: Kruskal constructs a minimum spanning tree using low-weight edges that avoid cycles.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, why should external input be parsed and validated?

options.A: To detect malformed or out-of-range values before use
options.B: To guarantee all input is trustworthy

questions.explanation: Validation checks whether input satisfies expected constraints.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a recursive algorithm makes one call on n-1 and constant extra work until the base case. What is its time complexity?
questions.explanation: There are n recursive levels with constant work per level.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is continuous integration?

options.A: Frequently integrate changes and run automated builds and tests

questions.explanation: CI provides fast automated feedback on integrated changes.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is deadlock?

options.A: A set of tasks waits indefinitely in a cycle for resources
options.C: A database query uses an index

questions.explanation: Deadlock occurs when cyclic resource waiting prevents progress.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the purpose of TLS in HTTPS?

options.A: Protect data in transit and authenticate the server in typical use

questions.explanation: TLS provides encryption and integrity and usually server authentication.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a foreign key for?

options.A: Represent or enforce a relationship to referenced key values

questions.explanation: Foreign keys help enforce referential integrity.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, why use a password-specific hashing algorithm with a unique salt?

options.A: Make offline password guessing harder after a database leak
options.B: Allow passwords to be read easily

questions.explanation: A salt and a deliberately costly password hash raise the cost of cracking.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is equivalence partitioning?

options.A: Grouping inputs expected to behave similarly and testing representatives

questions.explanation: Equivalence partitioning reduces test cases by selecting representative input classes.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, a class has unrelated responsibilities for billing, logging, and UI rendering. Which principle suggests splitting them?
questions.explanation: SRP favors one coherent responsibility per module.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which traversal gives sorted output from a valid binary search tree?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal visits keys in ascending order for a BST.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time and can be stable?
questions.explanation: Merge sort has O(n log n) worst-case time and a stable implementation is standard.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what does a boolean value represent?

options.A: A truth value such as true or false

questions.explanation: Boolean values represent logical truth states.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is the usual worst-case complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort has logarithmic levels and linear work per level.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, why write acceptance criteria?

options.A: Define observable conditions for a requirement to be considered complete

questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria make expectations clear and testable.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is virtual memory used for?

options.A: Provide virtual address spaces and manage mapping to physical memory

questions.explanation: Virtual memory abstracts physical memory and supports isolation and flexible allocation.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what does DHCP commonly provide?
questions.explanation: DHCP dynamically leases network configuration.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what does database normalization generally aim to reduce?
questions.explanation: Normalization structures relations to reduce duplication and anomalies.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is phishing?

options.A: A deceptive attempt to steal information or induce unsafe action

questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages or sites to trick victims.

questions.question: During a placement coding round, what is a flaky test?

options.A: A test with inconsistent outcomes under apparently unchanged conditions
options.B: A test that always passes reliably
